action.option: Route the 2005-2014 temperature change to substantial-change follow-up

unexecuted_proposal.brief_basis: chart_1 shows the 2005 value near 23.9 and the 2014 value near 10.1, a period-wide decrease of about 13.8; this is large enough for substantial-change follow-up under the task’s stated routing criterion.

rules.text: If the horizontal year labels bind the plotted markers to years, the vertical axis labeled "value" is a linear numeric scale with the printed ticks, and this chart is the dashboard record for the requested 2005-2014 temperature review, then the 2005 and 2014 marker heights can be decoded and compared to estimate the period-wide change. If the routing standard treats a change at least as large in magnitude as that estimate as substantial, the substantial-change follow-up option is supported.
rules.conditions: Requires that the plotted series is the relevant temperature record, that the axes encode the displayed years and values as assumed, and that the unspecified substantial-change standard includes the decoded endpoint change.

rules.text: If routing depends on whether the period-wide temperature change is "large enough" for targeted follow-up, a choice between substantial-change follow-up and routine monitoring requires a defined or otherwise verifiable standard for what counts as large enough; a qualitative criterion alone does not establish that classification.
rules.conditions: Applies because no numeric, categorical, or other decision threshold is supplied in the public task.

observations.location: plot title centered above the graph
observations.content: The visible title is "Global Temperature Change".
The horizontal axis is labeled "year"; its leftmost labeled tick is "2005" and its rightmost labeled tick is "2014", each with a blue circular marker above it.
The vertical axis is labeled "value" and has printed ticks 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, and 24. The 2005 marker is just below the 24 gridline, while the 2014 marker is just above the 10 gridline.

chains.claim: The chart visibly motivates checking a sizable endpoint difference, but the public task supplies no threshold or other verifiable definition distinguishing a substantial change from ordinary variation. Therefore the available evidence does not establish whether substantial-change follow-up or routine monitoring is the required route.

questions.question: Does any public instruction define “period-wide temperature change” as the net difference between the 2005 and 2014 endpoint markers, and specify that its magnitude rather than another whole-period measure is the routing input?
Is there any public condition that makes the archive-and-background-filing option eligible, or do the stated targeted-follow-up versus routine-monitoring criteria fully delimit the applicable routes?

counterquestions.summary: Inspected the plotted single line, year ticks from 2005 through 2014, endpoint positions against the labeled value scale, the chart title, and the task’s routing language. The existing chains cover conditional endpoint decoding and the absent substantial-versus-ordinary threshold; remaining limits concern the intended definition of period-wide change and whether the listed archive option has any stated applicability.
